prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1252; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder after a left-turn collision at an intersection. Claimant is represented by counsel, and the file has been opened for bodily injury and property damage review.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the policy records suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact. Witness statements, scene photos and the other driver's account all match the described sequence of events.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage is mostly consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record, and an appraiser is scheduled to confirm the repair scope.

Entry 5: Claimant has described the accident the same way in every contact so far. Shoulder injury is reported, but it is not yet clear whether it was caused by this crash. Prior medical history to the same area is not known at this stage.

Entry 6: Treatment records show a usual course of care, with visits tapering as the claimant's condition improved. Causation review is pending the medical file and an independent evaluation.

Entry 7: Counsel has been notified of the open items, including causation of the shoulder injury. Next step is to request complete treatment records and schedule a follow-up with the claimant's attorney.
